  <section id="how-it-works" class="flow-section content-width section-space" aria-labelledby="flow-title">
    <div class="section-heading"><p class="eyebrow">How it fits together</p><h2 id="flow-title">One project. Every part stays connected.</h2><p>Plots made with fluxplot keep a name on every part. Figures are composed from those plots, papers and slides are built from those figures, and references flow in from your library. One document, one deck: export them to whatever format the journal, the conference or your <span class="nowrap">co-author</span> needs.</p></div>
    <div class="flow" role="img" aria-label="Diagram: Library opens into Reader, and Reader's notes are cited in Paper. Python plots are imported into Figure; re-running the script updates the figure. Figures are placed and captioned in Paper and animated in Slides. Paper exports to Word, PDF, HTML and journal styles; Slides export to an HTML deck, PowerPoint, PDF handouts and video.">

One manuscript, every output format.</span></div></foreignObject>

        <foreignObject x="20" y="646" width="160" height="222"><div xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1999/xhtml" class="flow-box is-export"><span class="flow-box-title">Documents</span><span class="flow-box-note">One manuscript, any format.</span><span class="flow-formats"><span>Word</span><span>PDF</span><span>HTML</span><span>Journal styles</span></span></div></foreignObject>
        <foreignObject x="220" y="646" width="160" height="222"><div xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1999/xhtml" class="flow-box is-export"><span class="flow-box-title">Decks</span><span class="flow-box-note">One deck, any format.</span><span class="flow-formats"><span>HTML deck</span><span>PowerPoint</span><span>PDF handout</span><span>Video</span></span></div></foreignObject>
      </svg>
    </div>
    <ul class="flow-points">
      <li><strong>Plain files.</strong> Manuscripts are Quarto Markdown, references are BibTeX, figures and decks are readable JSON beside their SVGs. Keep the folder in git, open it in any editor, hand it to a colleague.</li>
      <li><strong>Live links.</strong> A plot placed in a figure stays linked to its source. Re-run the analysis and the regenerated plot hot-swaps into every figure, with your restyles intact.</li>
      <li><strong>Write once, export anywhere.</strong> A journal style is applied on the way out, never to your text, so switching from one journal to another or from PDF to Word is a menu choice.</li>
    </ul>
  </section>

  <section class="structure-section content-width section-space" aria-labelledby="structure-title">
    <div class="section-heading"><p class="eyebrow">Semantic plots</p><h2 id="structure-title">A plot is a structure, not a picture.</h2><p>Every meaningful part of a fluxplot plot carries a stable name. Hover the plot: a single point, the median line, the tick labels of an axis. That name is what you restyle in Figure, caption in Paper and animate in Slides, and it survives when the plot is regenerated.</p></div>

  <section id="slides" class="motion-showcase content-width section-space" aria-labelledby="motion-title">
    <div class="section-heading"><p class="eyebrow">Slides</p><h2 id="motion-title">Explain it in motion.</h2><p>In Flux, any figure can become a slide, because the underlying editor and files are the same. That makes it seamless and simple to take a figure you have already made and add motion: reveal a series, morph a chart from one condition to the next, turn a 3D structure. Every change is a step you trigger, and the deck exports as one self-contained HTML file.</p></div>
    <div class="scene-tabs" role="group" aria-label="Choose a scene" hidden>
      <button type="button" data-scene="1" aria-pressed="true"><span>Same cells, new stimulus</span><small>Data morph</small></button>
      <button type="button" data-scene="2" aria-pressed="false"><span>A structure in motion</span><small>3D turntable</small></button>
      <button type="button" data-scene="0" aria-pressed="false"><span>A population of responses</span><small>Reveal</small></button>
    </div>
    <div class="slide-demo" id="slide-demo" data-demo-src="/demos/data-morph/index.html" data-demo-scene="1">
      <button type="button" class="demo-launch" aria-label="Load the interactive scientific slides" data-demo-start><img src="/assets/media/slide-poster.svg" alt="A population atlas of 143 recorded visual neurons. Open the native Flux presentation to explore three scientific slides." width="1200" height="760" loading="lazy"><span class="demo-launch-prompt"><span class="play-disc" aria-hidden="true"><svg viewBox="0 0 24 24"><path d="m9 6 9 6-9 6Z" /></svg></span><span>Play the slides<small>Real Flux slides, running in your browser</small></span></span></button>
    </div>
    <div class="demo-caption"><p>Use the arrows to step through a scene, or pick another scene above. The player is Flux’s own.</p><a class="text-link" href="/docs/slides.html">Learn about Slides<span aria-hidden="true">→</span></a></div>

  </section>
